item.text:
**Assessment**
Mixed, leaning `yes on formal rule-setting`, but `no on the overall business environment`. Abiy’s 2024 government pushed real reforms for macro-fairness, SOE governance, and private-sector-led growth, but persistent emergency rule, conflict, and leverage-seeking regional moves undercut the predictability that entrepreneurs and investors need.

**Accepted Claims**
- [IMF Executive Board Approves Four-Year US$3.4 billion Extended Credit Facility Arrangement for Ethiopia](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/29/pr24291-ethiopia-imf-exec-board-approves-4yr-us3b-ecf-arr) | IMF | 2024-07-29 | The IMF said the reform agenda aimed to restore debt sustainability, end monetary financing, tighten monetary policy, mobilize revenue, and strengthen SOE finances. This supports a claim that Abiy pursued rule-based economic reform rather than arbitrary rent extraction. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`

- [The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia: Request of an Arrangement Under the Extended Credit Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/07/29/the-federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia-request-of-an-arrangement-under-the-extended-552778) | IMF | 2024-07-29 | The staff report tied reform to debt sustainability, inflation control, market-determined FX, prudent fiscal management, and SOE oversight including government-independent directors and an independent NBE supervisor. This is strong evidence for creating formal rules that should improve competition and investment conditions. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.2`

- [The National Bank of Ethiopia Announces the Launch of a New Monetary Policy Framework](https://nbe.gov.et/nbe_news/the-national-bank-of-ethiopia-announces-the-launch-of-a-new-monetary-policy-framework/) | National Bank of Ethiopia | 2024-07-09 | NBE said it was modernizing monetary policy around price stability, an interest-rate-based regime, and stronger technical capacity. This is direct evidence for a more predictable framework for trade, investment, and job creation. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.2`

- [The Council of Ministers today approved the draft NBE Proclamation and Banking Business Proclamation](https://nbe.gov.et/nbe_news/the-council-of-ministers-today-approved-the-draft-nbe-proclamation-and-banking-business-proclamation/) | National Bank of Ethiopia | 2024-06-14 | The draft laws were described as strengthening credibility, accountability, transparency, and governance in banking and the central bank. That points toward fairer institutional rules for finance and investment. | `5B.4`, `5B.2`, `4B.4`

- [World Bank Backs Ethiopia's Reforms to Promote Sustainable and Inclusive Growth, Enhance Resilience, and Take Climate Action](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/30/world-bank-backs-ethiopia-s-reforms-to-promote-sustainable-and-inclusive-afe-growth) | World Bank | 2024-07-30 | The World Bank said the package would improve fiscal transparency, public-spending effectiveness, SOE performance, private-sector orientation, financial stability, and social safety nets. This is strong evidence for a more rules-based environment for entrepreneurship and growth. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`

- [Ethiopia signs 1.72 billion USD Financing Agreements with the World Bank](https://www.mofed.gov.et/blog/ethiopia-signs-172-billion-usd-financing-agreements-with-the-world-bank/) | Ethiopia Ministry of Finance | 2024-04-05 | The ministry said the projects funded rural connectivity, food security, adaptive safety nets, power-sector reform, and water/sanitation. These are public-good investments that support broad job creation and market access rather than narrow elite capture. | `5B.4`, `5B.1`, `5B.3`

- [Landlocked Ethiopia signs pact to use Somaliland's Red Sea port](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Landlocked-Ethiopia-signs-pact-to-use-Somaliland-s-Red-Sea-port-45654814/) | Reuters | 2024-01-01 | Reuters reported the Berbera deal tied port access to possible recognition and naval use, which was widely treated as leverage-seeking and destabilizing. This is negative evidence against fair, predictable rules for trade and investment. | `5B.4`, `4B.10`, `5B.1`

- [Ethiopia extends state of emergency in Amhara](https://kelo.com/2024/02/02/ethiopia-extends-state-of-emergency-in-amhara/) | Reuters | 2024-02-02 | Parliament extended emergency rule amid insurgency and heavy casualties. That signals an unstable operating environment, which weakens fair entrepreneurship and long-term investment conditions even if reform laws exist on paper. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `4B.10`

- [Ethiopia’s authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/) | Amnesty International | 2024-02-19 | Amnesty said emergency powers were used for warrantless arrests, movement limits, and bans on assemblies and associations. This is indirect but important negative evidence because it undermines predictable rules and protected commercial activity. | `5B.4`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find strong direct 2024 evidence of a clean property-rights reform, anti-corruption competition law, or broad deregulatory package that can be shown to have been fully implemented.
- The best positive evidence is mostly IMF/NBE/World Bank institutional reform language plus some financing for public goods.
- The main counterweight is that conflict and emergency governance still made the rules environment unpredictable, so the answer is `partial reform, but not a clearly fair or stable rule system overall`.
